 Kyrie Irving trade being monitored by Miami Heat, but there's a catch 
 2026-10-29 00:44 
 The Miami Heat are expected to monitor Kyrie Irving, but their lack of assets will be challenging to pull a potential trade, per Shams Charania.
 Credit: AP - Scanpix 
 Credit AP - Scanpix 
 Credit AP - Scanpix

 The Miami Heat could position themselves for a Kyrie Irving trade, but they face a significant hurdle in executing a potential deal.

 Shams Charania of ESPN doubts the Heat's chances of acquiring Irving due to their lack of assets available to convince the Dallas Mavericks.
 "I'm sure, knowing the Heat, they're going to be monitoring Kyrie Irving, but there's going to be several teams eyeing Kyrie Irving. The question is, if you're Miami, what can you give for Kyrie Irving? You already traded away three first-round picks and a swap and other assets to go get Giannis Antetokounmpo to bring to this team," Charania said on The Pat McAfee Show. "So, what can you trade?
 "Right now, I believe they have one first-round pick eligible to be traded. Is that enough to get Kyrie Irving? My sense is probably not. I think the price would be higher than that."
 Miami Heat monitoring Kyrie Irving?
 The Miami Heat find themselves in a rough and disappointing start, beginning their 2026-27 NBA season with an 0-4 record entering Wednesday's game against the Atlanta Hawks.
 After an offseason filled with hype and expectations upon landing Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Heat are suddenly struggling on both ends of the court.
 It would be intriguing to see how the Heat will continue to monitor Kyrie Irving especially if their downslide continues. However, they truly lack assets to offer after the blockbuster deal for Antetokounmpo.
 Besides, the Dallas Mavericks have not shown any interest in trading Irving away so far, as the star point guard is finally playing after missing the whole 2025-26 season due to a torn ACL injury.
 Only time will tell how things will unfold, as the Heat continue their hunt for that elusive first win of the season while Irving is still playing productive basketball with the Mavs as Cooper Flagg's co-star.
